If some pieces do not pass through, transfer them back to the trough and rub them again, adding a little flour. When we have passed all the mixture through, transfer the trahanas onto a clean sheet or tablecloth and spread it out on a bed or a large table in a shady place away from flies or other bugs. If this is not possible, cover it with tulle. Spread it in a thin layer so that it can dry. We leave it for about three or four days, stirring it occasionally. When it has dried, we pass it through the sifting screen to remove the excess flour and place it in a cloth bag or a glass jar.

Bent-over Barbell Row with an Overhand Grip
Starting position: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and slightly bend your knees. Hinge forward at the hips, maintaining a natural curve in your spine. Pull your shoulders away from your ears and keep your head in a straight line with your spine. Grasp the barbell with an overhand, shoulder-width grip, and lift it to just above your knees.
Execution: Exhale and use your back muscles to pull the barbell towards your hips. Then, controllably return the barbell to the position just above your knees and continue with the next repetition.
Common mistakes: Rounding the back, locking the knees, insufficient forward lean, and limited range of motion.
Muscles activated: Primarily the chest, glutes, arms, and triceps. Secondarily the back muscles (including the latissimus dorsi) and the hamstrings.
